predecessor.comparison: Famennian stem tetrapod (Ichthyostega horizon), not a second Eryops chronospecies

chronoseries.successor_note: Eryops series length is 1. Amniote epidermal scales are a later regime and are not assigned this slot's wavelength.

schnakenberg: du/dt = D_u lap u + gamma (a - u + u^2 v)
dv/dt = D_v lap v + gamma (b - u^2 v)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = gamma (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic on a flat 96 x 96 patch; not a curved skull roof

parameters.note: Reference diffusivities are scaled by (12 / lambda_ref)^2 so the linear wavelength is 12 pixels = 127 µm. These are not the Loop_1217 organ-scale parameters.

empirical_claims: Turing 1952: a reaction-diffusion instability selects a finite critical wavenumber k_c.
Schnakenberg 1979: the two-species quadratic system used here has a stable homogeneous state that can be diffusion-driven unstable.
Witzmann, Scholz, Müller and Kardjilov 2010: basal tetrapod dermal bones carry a sculptured, vascularised ornament. This slot models one primordium wavelength of that ornament class at 127 µm.
Pawley and Warren 2006: the appendicular skeleton of Eryops megacephalus Cope, 1877 is Early Permian (Lower Permian of North America).
The AMNH photograph identifies the mount. It does not resolve 127 µm, and the script does not claim that it does.
